paper_metadata.title: Predictive ability of preinjury stressful life events and post-traumatic stress symptoms for outcomes following mild traumatic brain injury: analysis in a prospective emergency room sample

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study used a prospective, consecutive recruitment strategy from a Level I trauma center. Inclusion/exclusion criteria are clearly defined, and the baseline sample is well-described with demographic and clinical data. The participation rate (222/271 = 82%) is high.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: All participants for this study were recruited from consecutive admissions during specific time intervals to the EC of Ben Taub General Hospital, a Level I trauma centre in Houston, Texas
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly identified as emergency center admissions at a specific Level I trauma center.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: recruited from consecutive admissions during specific time intervals to the EC
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment is a gold standard for minimizing selection bias in prognosis studies.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: sustained a mTBI as defined by the Brain Injury Interdisciplinary Special Interest Group of the American Congress of Rehabilitation Medicine... Exclusion criteria included a history or diagnosis of the following conditions: a previous head injury requiring hospitalisation...
items.reasoning: Detailed clinical criteria (GCS, LOC, neuroimaging) and specific exclusion criteria (prior TBI, CNS disorders, major psychiatric illness) are provided.

items.evidence_snippet: Of 271 persons meeting eligibility criteria, 222 provided informed consent and completed a baseline assessment
items.reasoning: The participation rate is 81.9%, which exceeds the common 80% threshold for low risk.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The follow-up rate was 84%, and the authors performed a statistical comparison between completers and non-completers, finding no significant differences in baseline characteristics, which suggests attrition was not informative.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Of the 222 participants who completed the baseline assessment, 186 (84%) completed the 3-month outcome assessment.
items.reasoning: An 84% follow-up rate is considered high for a trauma sample.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: There were no significant differences between participants who did (N=186) and did not (N=36) complete the outcome assessment with respect to age, education, gender, race, presence or absence of findings on neuroimaging, and scores on preinjury measures
items.reasoning: The authors explicitly compared the characteristics of those lost to follow-up against those who completed the study.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: as shown by independent samples t tests and Pearson χ2.
items.reasoning: Statistical testing confirmed no significant differences between the groups.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (SLESQ and PCL) are validated tools, but they rely on retrospective recall of pre-injury status measured within 2 weeks post-injury. This introduces a risk of recall bias, as the injury itself or early post-concussive symptoms might influence the reporting of pre-injury stress.

items.evidence_snippet: Stressful Life Events Questionnaire (SLESQ)... PTSD Checklist (PCL)... The total incidence score was used in the current analyses
items.reasoning: The PFs are defined by specific, validated psychometric instruments.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: participants were asked to respond to questions according to symptoms experienced during the month prior to injury... SLESQ has been shown to have adequate test—retest reliability and validity.
items.reasoning: While the tools are valid, the study relies entirely on retrospective recall after a brain injury, which is a known source of measurement bias.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes were measured using standardized, validated instruments (SF-36 and BSI) at a consistent 3-month time point. The use of oral administration by research assistants ensured consistency across the sample.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Outcomes were assessed at 3 months after injury and included the depression and anxiety subscales of the Brief Symptom Inventory, and the physical and mental component scores of the 36-item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36).
items.reasoning: The outcomes and the follow-up window are explicitly defined.

items.evidence_snippet: internal consistency and test—retest estimates range from 0.89 to 0.94... Adequate internal consistency has been demonstrated by Cronbach α coefficients of 0.85
items.reasoning: The authors cite established psychometric properties for the SF-36 and BSI.

items.evidence_snippet: All measures were administered orally to the participant by an English- or Spanish-speaking research assistant.
items.reasoning: The administration method was standardized.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study used hierarchical regression to control for critical confounders including age, injury severity (complicated vs. uncomplicated), and pre-injury depression (CES-D). This addresses the most likely factors that could distort the relationship between life events and outcomes.
